ideal: Bd5 allows Nxd5 and Bxf2+, losing the f2-pawn and forcing the king to e2.
note: The bishop-knight exchange is followed by a pawn capture with check that costs White castling.

ideal: a5 allows e5, after which Nxe5 fxe5 fxe5 gives up the d7-knight for two pawns.
note: The knight sacrifice and the later g5 mate threat after h4 are separate costs.

ideal: Nxe5 loses the f3-knight for the e5-pawn after Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nxe5.
note: The lost knight is decisive; losing castling in the queen exchange is incidental.

ideal: Bd6 allows Qxg7 and Qxh8+, losing the h8-rook and both kingside pawns for the g1-knight.
note: The h8 capture also forces Ke7, but the material loss is already a sufficient reason.

ideal: Rb8 misses Ra1, which decoys the queen onto a1 for the knight fork Nc2+ and Nxa1.
note: The check wins time to take the queen; the c4-pawn falls later with Bxc4.

ideal: Rxh7 allows Nd6+, forking the king and b7-queen, which falls to Nxb7+.
note: The fork wins the queen for the h7-bishop, with the b4-pawn recovered later.

ideal: Kh8 allows Rxg5 to take the queen with a mate threat on f6, after which f6 lets the rook escape with Rgg1.
note: Both lines surrender the queen, but the mate threat explains the rook surviving in the played line.

ideal: Qg5 misses Bxh3, when Qg4 threatens mate on g2 and drives the king to f1 before Qxg2+.
note: The mate threat on g2 is real and accompanies the capture of the h3- and g2-pawns.

ideal: Rb2 allows Rd8+ and Qc5, threatening mate on h5 and forcing Kg6 before Qxc8 takes the bishop.
note: Qc5 attacks the c8-bishop while the mate threat makes Black spend a move on the king.

ideal: Bxg1 misses Bg3, whose mate threat on f2 induces Qe1 and lets Bxe1 win the queen for a bishop.
note: Bxg1 also threatens Qf2#, so that threat alone does not distinguish the moves.

ideal: Bf3 misses Be2, preserving the mate threat on h4 without allowing Bxf3 and winning the b7-bishop after Qc7 Rhf8 Qxb7.
note: Both bishop moves threaten Qh4#, but only Bf3 lets the b7-bishop exchange off the attacker.

ideal: gxh4 misses Qxg8+, followed by Qg7+ and Qxh6, winning the g8-knight and h6-rook.
note: The checks force the king out while the queen collects the knight and rook; fxg3 later also takes the bishop.

ideal: Nb4 allows Qxg6+ and Bc4, threatening mate on h6 and provoking the queen sacrifice Qa6 Bxa6.
note: The queen sacrifice diverts the bishop from c4 and gives the king the g8 escape square.

ideal: Nxc6 allows Qd6 with a mate threat on h2, forcing Bg3 and leaving the c6-knight to Qxc6.
note: The mate threat takes priority over saving the knight.

ideal: Qc5 misses Qxd2, which takes the d2-knight with a mate threat on d1.
note: The knight capture is backed by a real back-rank mating threat and the rooks on the c-file.

ideal: Bxc2 allows Nxe6 with a mate threat on d8, and Rxd1 Bxd1 fxe6 costs a rook for a knight and pawn.
note: The queens cancel in the exchanges, leaving Black down a rook for the e6-knight and c2-pawn.

ideal: a6 allows Nd5 and Nxc7+, forking the king and a8-rook, which falls to Nxa8.
note: The pawn claim is true but incomplete: the checking fork also wins the rook and costs castling.

ideal: Qg5 misses Nxb6, whose mate threat on f7 prevents a pawn recapture and lets the knight take a8 after Ne6 Bxe6 fxe6.
note: The full line yields a rook and pawn for a knight, not for a bishop.

ideal: Be6 misses Qc3, threatening mate on e1 and taking the a3-bishop after h3.
note: The queen attacks the bishop while its mate threat forces White to make an escape square.

ideal: Qe2 misses Qa5, whose mate threat on c7 induces Nb6, allowing Nxb6+ cxb6 Qxa7 to win a pawn.
note: The mating threat draws the knight to b6 and opens the route to the a7-pawn.

ideal: h6 allows Nxe5, taking the e5-pawn with a mate threat on f7.
note: The mate threat is genuine, and the given reply d5 blocks the c4-bishop.

ideal: Bc8 allows e6 with a mate threat on g7, and Bf6 Bxf6 Qxf6 exf7+ Qxf7 Bxf7+ wins the queen for a bishop.
note: The mate defense brings the queen to f6, where the pawn advance forces it onto the b3-bishop diagonal.

ideal: f3 allows Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nf2+, forking the king and h1-rook, which falls to Nxh1.
note: The checking knight fork explains the rook loss; castling rights are secondary.

ideal: Nge2 misses fxe5, which takes the e5-knight.
note: No white pawn is lost in the best line, whose exchanges leave White a bishop ahead on captures.

ideal: b3 allows Nxe3 to take the e3-pawn with an attack on the queen, followed by Nxd3 taking another pawn.
note: The pawn losses are the material point; White also moves its king in the best line.

ideal: Qc2 allows Nxd3+ followed by Qxf3, losing both minor pieces with a mate threat on h1.
note: The captures of the bishop, knight and g3-pawn are real, and Qxf3 also threatens mate.

ideal: Kg7 misses Bxa8, which takes the undefended a8-rook.
note: Kg7 also threatens Rd1#, while Bxa8 simply removes a whole rook and retains the attack.

ideal: Bd6 misses Qxc3, taking the c3-bishop before Qxh3 threatens mate on h2.
note: The pawn claim is incomplete because Qxc3 also takes a bishop; the later mating threat is real.

ideal: Kb1 misses Bb6, when Bb5+ and Bxa4 Bxa4 Qxa4+ win the a-pawn.
note: The minor-piece exchanges cancel, leaving the a-pawn won; the later king recapture is incidental.

ideal: Nf4 allows Qc6 and Nxf4 with a mate threat on g2, then Qxc6 Nxh3+ gxh3 Bxc6 costs the h3-pawn.
note: The mate threat prevents recapturing on f4, and the checking zwischenzug wins h3 before the queens come off.
